title: Local implementer: sliver a larger slice first
lead: *Proposed.* Owner decision 2026-11-12 (relay session 8d711f67, chat): "if we're using local we should sliver a larger slice to break it down." When the owner runs a slice on a local implementer, ork first has it carved into slivers (rule u6, one or two files each, effort 1), and the local implementer runs the slivers one after another in the parent's worktree (adj 124, S62).
findings_note: S304 trials 1 and 2: a claude-local implementer could not finish a size S ork slice in 45 or 90 minutes; its context grew past 80k tokens while it explored.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: *Proposed.* Owner decision 2026-11-12 (relay session 8d711f67, chat): "if we're using local we should sliver a larger slice to break it down." A local implementer needs a task small enough to finish within its context and time. When the owner runs a slice above size S on a local implementer, ork first has it carved into slivers (rule u6, one or two files each, size S, effort 1), and the local implementer runs the slivers one after another in the parent's worktree (adj 124, S62, `ork run PARENT --slivers`). Recorded decisions: the cloud spec check row carves the slivers and ork files them with no owner confirmation (adj 337, `roles.local-sliver-carver`); every slice above size S is slivered (adj 338, `roles.local-sliver-when`).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- A local run of a size M slice has slivers carved by the spec check and filed with no owner confirmation, then the plan lists them and runs the chain (`TestLocalRunOfASizeMSliceCarvesAndFilesSliversThenRunsTheChain`).
- A confirmed set of slivers runs as one chain in the parent's worktree on the local implementer (`TestLocalRunOfASlicedSliceRunsItsSliversAsOneChainInTheParentWorktree`).
- A cloud-implementer run of the same slice is not slivered (`TestCloudRunOfASizeMSliceIsNotSlivered`).
- A local run of an effort 3 slice is refused and tells the owner to pick a cloud implementer (`TestLocalRunOfAnEffortThreeSliceIsRefused`).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Build the carving step and wire it in front of S62's chain (S62 has landed), test first.
2. Docs (*proposed*): `docs/design.md`. CHANGELOG.md: one bullet under `## Unreleased`.

Owner decisions (2026-11-16): Which cloud role carves the slivers, and how does its result become sliver items? -> spec-check-row: reuse the spec check row (r16) with a new carve prompt; the role stays read-only and writes a sliver list (title, files, tests and checks per sliver) in its report, and ork files each item with `slicer add --parent PARENT --size S --effort 1` through a new `Parent` field on `AddSpec` (`internal/slicercli/write.go`) [roles.local-sliver-carver-role]. What does ork do when a slice above size S is not eligible to sliver under contract rule u6 (effort 3 never; effort 2 only if every sliver is effort 1)? -> refuse-local: ork refuses to run a non-slivered size M or L slice, or an effort 3 slice, on a local implementer and tells the owner to pick a cloud implementer [roles.local-sliver-ineligible]. How should the stale spec text match the recorded decisions (adj 337 cloud-auto, adj 338 above-s)? -> rewrite: the Why drops the open questions and records 337 and 338. Failing test 1 becomes "a local run of a size M slice has slivers carved and filed with no owner confirmation, then runs the chain". Files drops "if Q1 is (a)". Implement step 1 drops the `adj ask`.

Owner decisions (2026-11-16): When does the carve run, and does the owner approve the plan before ork files the slivers? -> in-spec-check: the carve runs inside the spec check that ork already runs before every start; ork files the slivers from its report, and the chain plan then lists them for the owner's one approval (adj 388) [roles.local-sliver-carve-timing, adj 396]. Rework (owner, 2026-11-16, 'Rework before landing'): round 1 carved at the start after a plan that showed only 'carve', and ran the chain with no listed slivers to approve. Move the carve into the spec check and show the filed slivers in the chain plan for the one approval; update docs/design.md and the tests to match.
